top_story.headline: Committee tells the FEC it fixed a $5,000 contribution to Rep. Ken Calvert's campaign that was wrongly labeled as a primary gift
top_story.dek: Maintaining All Republicans In Office PAC answered an October 13 request for additional information by amending its year-end report.
paragraphs: Maintaining All Republicans In Office PAC told the FEC in a Form 99 received October 17 that it re-designated a $5,000 contribution to Ken Calvert for Congress. The contribution had been attributed to the primary election when it should have been a general election gift for 2026.
The PAC says it amended its January 31, 2026 Year-End report to show the general election designation and filed it with the FEC. The Form 99 is a response to an RFAI dated October 13, 2026.

The filing is a routine correction of an election designation, and it shows no sign of wrongdoing. No new RFAI letters surfaced in this batch, and no red-flag keywords or voided transactions turned up.

sections.headline: One sitting member's campaign filed a correction
paragraphs: One filing in this batch is tagged to a sitting lawmaker. It is a routine amendment note.

items: Rep. Keith Self (R-TX) tells the FEC his campaign amended its Q1 2026 report to split 2 refunded contributions between elections. Self for Congress says the amendment changed no cash totals. The filing was received 10/17. (Form 99)

sections.headline: Eight small committees file Form 99s, mostly saying they fall below filing thresholds
paragraphs: Most of these are zero-activity or below-threshold notices from small candidate and PAC committees. One is a response to an RFAI, and one is a long-shot presidential candidate describing a mailed paper report.

items: Maintaining All Republicans In Office PAC tells the FEC it re-designated a $5,000 contribution to Ken Calvert for Congress from the primary to the 2026 general election. It says it amended its Year-End report in response to an RFAI dated October 13. This is a PAC. (Form 99)

John Rice for President says it has not raised or spent more than $5,000 for the October Quarterly period, and that it mailed a paper Form 3P on October 8. The presidential candidate, Jonathon Mark Rice, says he has had no confirmation of receipt and asks the FEC to confirm that the Form 99 clears a Late File Notification. He gives an updated address in Los Angeles. This is a candidate committee. (Form 99)

David McCauley for President tells the FEC it has raised $0.00 and describes a 2040 presidential run under the name Team America 2040. The filing is a public message from the candidate, and it says a DonorBox fundraising page has raised nothing. This is a candidate committee. (Form 99)
Dreadnought PAC reports $0 in contributions and $0 in disbursements for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Treasurer Ian Cluroe signed the note. This is a PAC. (Form 99)

C Monday for Liberty tells the FEC the campaign has not raised or spent $50,000. The filing is from an open-seat Tennessee House candidate, Christopher Brian Monday, who is running as an unaffiliated candidate. The filing says $50,000 where the usual threshold is $5,000. This is a candidate committee. (Form 99)
Jose Vera for Congress tells the FEC it has not met the $5,000 threshold. The Wisconsin Republican challenger's committee gave no other detail. This is a candidate committee. (Form 99)

StockForCongress tells the FEC it has not reached the $5,000 required for submission. The committee belongs to Eustaquio Castro-Mendoza, a Texas Democratic challenger. This is a candidate committee. (Form 99)
Supporters of Catherine Hildebrand reports $0 raised and $0 spent. The committee supports a Washington state Democratic challenger. This is a candidate committee. (Form 99)
